title: Which change fixes the loop?
statement:
This loop is supposed to print the chance of **at least one six** in n rolls of a die, for n = 1 to 4:

```python
for n in range(1, 5):
    print(n, round(1 - (1/6)**n, 3))
```

It prints numbers that are far too big. Which single change makes it correct?

[_]{a}

explanations: $1 - n/6$ goes negative after 6 rolls, so it can't be a probability.
Correct. $(5/6)^n$ is the chance of **no** six in n rolls; 1 minus it is the chance of at least one.
That only changes which n values print; the formula is still wrong.
$(1/6)^n$ is the chance that **every** roll is a six.

hints: What is the complement of "at least one six"?
"No six" in one roll has probability 5/6, not 1/6.
Only the base of the power needs to change.
solution:
The complement of "at least one six in n rolls" is "no six in n rolls", probability $(5/6)^n$. The fixed loop prints:

```text
1 0.167
2 0.306
3 0.421
4 0.518
```
